script_nghe: Urbanisation. Roughly fifty-seven per cent of the world’s population now lives in urban areas. The fastest growth is no longer in megacities but in secondary cities — places of one to five million. The main driver remains economic opportunity, as it has been for two centuries. The largest infrastructure gap is sanitation, ahead of transport and housing, though it receives the least attention. Estimates for the investment required run to around ninety-four trillion dollars by twenty forty. My criticism of past planning is that it focused too heavily on transport, at the expense of basic services. If I had to name one priority, it would be water and sanitation. Our case study will be Indonesia. And the reading list is on the department website, not the course portal.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Checkpoint cuối — full test Speaking 14 phút, mục tiêu band 6.0–6.5.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 1 (4–5 phút) — Work, study, free time
cau_tra_loi.mau:
Q: What do you do?
A: I work in e-commerce for an electronics retailer. My role involves managing website content and increasingly automating our data processes.

Q: Do you enjoy it?
A: Most of it, yes. The part I find most satisfying is building tools that save the team time — less so the coordination between departments.

Q: Are you studying anything at the moment?
A: English, seriously for the first time in years. I'm working towards a test in November, and after that I'm hoping to apply for a master's programme.

Q: What do you do in your free time?
A: Reading and cycling, mainly. I go out on the bike twice a week, usually at the weekend when the roads are quieter.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Part 1: mỗi câu 20–30 giây. Trả lời trực tiếp rồi thêm một chi tiết. Đừng nói dài.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 2 (2 phút) — Describe a skill you would like to improve
cau_tra_loi.mau:
I'd like to talk about public speaking, or more precisely presenting in English.

It's something I need for work. I present data and proposals to management fairly regularly, and while I can do it in Vietnamese without much thought, in English I become noticeably more hesitant.

The difficulty isn't vocabulary — it's that I'm translating while speaking, which slows everything down. Having noticed that, I've started preparing in English from the beginning rather than writing in Vietnamese and converting.

I'd like to reach the point where I can handle unexpected questions confidently. Prepared material is manageable; it's the follow-up questions that expose you.

If I improved this, I think it would make the most difference to my career of anything I could learn right now.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Dàn ý Part 2: kỹ năng gì → vì sao cần → khó ở đâu → mục tiêu → hệ quả. Năm phần × ~25 giây. Dùng mệnh đề rút gọn (Having noticed), cấu trúc nhấn mạnh (it's the follow-up questions that…), điều kiện loại 2 (If I improved…).

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Part 3 (4–5 phút) — Skills, learning, the future of work
cau_tra_loi.mau:
Q: Why do some people learn languages faster than others?
A: Exposure more than talent, I'd say. People who learn quickly are usually those who use the language daily rather than studying it in isolation. Motivation matters too — if you need it for something concrete, you progress much faster.

Q: Should companies pay for employee training?
A: It's in their interest, certainly. Training reduces turnover, which is expensive. The objection is that trained staff may leave — but staff who aren't developing leave anyway, so the argument doesn't really hold.

Q: Will people need to retrain more often in future?
A: Almost certainly. The assumption that you train once and work for forty years is already outdated. What worries me is that education systems are still built around that assumption.

Q: Is it ever too late to learn something new?
A: Practically, rarely. It's slower, and you have less time to recover the investment — that's a real constraint at forty rather than twenty. But the main obstacle I've seen is people deciding in advance that it's too late.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Part 3: mỗi câu 35–45 giây. Có phản biện chính lập luận ("the argument doesn't really hold"), cấu trúc nhấn mạnh (What worries me is…), và câu chốt cá nhân ở cuối.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Part 1 ngắn gọn, Part 2 nói liền 2 phút không vấp, Part 3 mỗi câu 35–45 giây có lập luận nhiều lớp.
coordination · hesitant · exposure · in isolation · turnover · outdated · constraint · recover the investment.

Mệnh đề rút gọn (Having noticed) · nhấn mạnh (it's the follow-up questions that expose you · What worries me is) · điều kiện loại 2 (If I improved this, it would make…) · bị động (are still built around).
hesitant /ˈhezɪtənt/ · coordination /kəʊˌɔːdɪˈneɪʃn/ · constraint /kənˈstreɪnt/. Chú ý nối âm: "it's the follow-up questions that expose you" → "tha-tex-POSE-you".

meo_noi: Đây là checkpoint cuối khoá. Nói trôi cả ba phần trong 14 phút là bạn đã đạt mục tiêu band 6.0–6.5.
GHI ÂM toàn bộ bài này và so với file ghi âm ở unit 8 — bài đầu tiên bạn ghi ở Level 0. Đó là bằng chứng rõ nhất về chặng đường đã đi.
Ba thứ phân biệt band 6 và band 7 trong bài này: (1) trả lời có sắc thái chứ không tuyệt đối, (2) tự phản biện lập luận của mình, (3) dùng 2–3 cấu trúc phức tạp một cách tự nhiên chứ không cố ý.
Sau checkpoint này: chuyển sang luyện đề Cambridge IELTS 15–19 và đăng ký thi thật.
